plan: 1 Kings 3:16-28; 1 Kings 5:1-18; 2 Chronicles 2:1-18; 1 Kings 6:1-13; 2 Chronicles 3:1-14; 1 Kings 6:14-38

readings.title: The Two Whores and the Dead Child
readings.subtitle: A complex case of deception is brought before the earthly throne.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 3:16] Then two women, whores, came to the sovereign, and stood before him.
[17] And one woman said, “O my master, this woman and I dwell in the same house. And I gave birth while she was in the house.
[18] “And it came to be, the third day after I had given birth, that this woman also gave birth. And we were together. There was no one else with us in the house, only the two of us in the house.
[19] “Then this woman’s son died in the night, because she lay on him.
[20] “And she rose up in the middle of the night and took <dn>את</dn> my son from my side, while your female servant slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid <dn>את</dn> her dead child in my bosom.
[21] “And I rose up in the morning to nurse <dn>את</dn> my son and saw he was dead. But I looked at him closely in the morning, and saw he was not my son whom I had borne.”
[22] And the other woman said, “No! But the living one is my son, and the dead one is your son.” And the first woman said, “No! For the dead one is your son, and the living one is my son.” And they spoke before the sovereign.

readings.title: The Sword of True Discernment
readings.subtitle: Shelomoh wields divine wisdom to expose the origin of true maternal compassion.
readings.text:
[23] And the sovereign said, “The one says, ‘This is my son, who lives, and your son is the dead one,’ while the other says, ‘No! For your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’ ”
[24] And the sovereign said, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought a sword before the sovereign.
[25] And the sovereign said, “Divide <dn>את</dn> the living child in two, and give half to one, and half to the other.”
[26] And the woman whose son was living spoke to the sovereign, for she was overcome with compassion for her son. And she said, “O my master, give her <dn>את</dn> the living child, and by no means kill him!” But the other said, “Let him be neither mine nor yours, but divide him.”
[27] And the sovereign answered and said, “Give the first woman <dn>את</dn> the living child, and by no means kill him – she is his mother.”
[28] And all Yisra’ěl heard of <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling which the sovereign had rendered. And they feared the sovereign, for they saw that the wisdom of <dn>Elohim</dn> was in him to do right-ruling.

readings.title: The Intent to House the Name
readings.subtitle: Shelomoh declares a time of rest to execute the covenantal promise to Daviḏ.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 5:1] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent his servants to Shelomoh, because he heard that they had anointed him sovereign in place of his father, for Ḥiram had always loved Daviḏ.
[2] And Shelomoh sent to Ḥiram, saying,
[3] “You know my father Daviḏ was unable to build a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> because of <dn>את</dn> the battles which were all around him, until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put <dn>את</dn> them under the soles of his feet.
[4] “But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn> has given me rest all around, there is neither adversary nor evil incident.
[5] “And see, I intend to build a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to my father Daviḏ, saying, ‘Your son, whom <dn>I</dn> set on your throne in your place, he does build <dn>את</dn> the house for <dn>My</dn> Name.’
[6] “And now, command that they cut down cedars for me from Leḇanon. And let my servants be with your servants, and let me pay you wages for your servants according to whatever you say. For you know there is none among us who knows to cut timber like the Tsiḏonians.”

readings.title: A Covenant of Timber and Grain
readings.subtitle: The King of Tsor rejoices at the wisdom of YeHoVaH placed upon Daviḏ’s heir.
readings.text:
[7] And it came to be, when Ḥiram heard the words of Shelomoh, that he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this day, for <dn>He</dn> has given Daviḏ a wise son over this great people!”
[8] And Ḥiram sent to Shelomoh, saying, “I have heard <dn>את</dn> that which you sent me. Let me do all you desire concerning the cedar and cypress logs.
[9] “Let my servants bring them down from Leḇanon to the sea, then I put <dn>את</dn> them in rafts by sea to the place you direct me. And I shall spread them out there, then you take <dn>את</dn> them up, while you do my desire by giving food for my household.”
[10] And Ḥiram gave Shelomoh cedar and cypress logs – all his desire.
[11] And Shelomoh gave Ḥiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty kors of pressed oil. Thus Shelomoh gave to Ḥiram year by year.
[12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Shelomoh wisdom, as <dn>He</dn> promised him. And there was peace between Ḥiram and Shelomoh, and the two of them made a covenant.

readings.title: Mobilizing the Builders
readings.subtitle: Tens of thousands are conscripted to execute the heavy labor of construction.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 5:13] And Sovereign Shelomoh raised up compulsory labour out of all Yisra’ěl. And the compulsory labour was thirty thousand men.
[14] And he sent them to Leḇanon, ten thousand per new moon by courses – they were one new moon in Leḇanon, two new moons at home. And Aḏoniram was over the compulsory labour.
[15] And Shelomoh had seventy thousand bearing burdens, and eighty thousand hewing stone in the mountains,
[16] besides three thousand three hundred from the chiefs of Shelomoh’s deputies who were over the work, those ruling over the people who laboured in the work.

readings.title: Hewing the Foundation Stones
readings.subtitle: Massive, precious stones are meticulously cut to anchor the House.
readings.text:
[17] And the sovereign commanded, and they brought large stones, precious stones, to lay <dn>את</dn> the foundation of the House with hewn stones.
[18] And Shelomoh’s builders, and Ḥiram’s builders, and the men of Geḇal did hew, and prepared <dn>את</dn> timber and <dn>את</dn> stones to build <dn>את</dn> the House.

readings.title: Enrolling the Burden Bearers
readings.subtitle: The sheer magnitude of the project requires massive human infrastructure.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 2:1] And Shelomoh gave word to build a House for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and a house for his reign.
[2] Then Shelomoh enrolled seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand hewing stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.

readings.title: A Requisition for Master Craftsmanship
readings.subtitle: Shelomoh acknowledges that the House cannot contain Elohim, serving only as a place of offering.
readings.text:
[3] And Shelomoh sent to Ḥuram sovereign of Tsor, saying, “As you did for my father Daviḏ, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in –
[4] see, I am building a House for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, to set it apart to <dn>Him</dn>, to burn before <dn>Him</dn> sweet incense, and for the continual showbread, and for the ascending offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. This is for Yisra’ěl forever.
[5] “And the House which I build is great, for our <dn>Elohim</dn> is greater than all mighty ones.
[6] “But who is able to build <dn>Him</dn> a House, since the heavens and the heavens of the heavens are unable to contain <dn>Him</dn>? Who am I then, that I should build <dn>Him</dn> a House, except to offer before <dn>Him</dn>?
[7] “And now, send me at once a man who knows to work in gold, and in silver, and in bronze, and in iron, and in purple and crimson and blue, and knowing to engrave with the skilled men who are with me in Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, whom Daviḏ my father has prepared.
[8] “And send me cedar, cypress and algum logs from Leḇanon, for I know that your servants know to cut timber in Leḇanon. And see, my servants are with your servants,
[9] even to prepare plenty of timber for me, for the House that I am building is great and marvellous.
[10] “And see, I have given servants to you, the hewers who cut timber, twenty thousand kors of ground wheat, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”

readings.title: Tsor Recognizes the Creator
readings.subtitle: Ḥuram formally blesses the Elohim of Yisra’ěl for His sovereignty over the earth.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 2:11] Then Ḥuram the sovereign of Tsor answered in writing, which he sent to Shelomoh, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> loves <dn>His</dn> people, <dn>He</dn> has made you sovereign over them.”
[12] And Ḥuram said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, who made the heavens and earth, for <dn>He</dn> has given Sovereign Daviḏ a wise son, knowing wisdom and understanding, to build a House for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and a house for his reign!

readings.title: The Dispatch of Ḥuram-Aḇi
readings.subtitle: A highly skilled artisan is deployed to manage the intricate physical elements of the temple.
readings.text:
[13] “And now I have sent a skilled man having understanding, Ḥuram-aḇi,
[14] the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tsor, who knows to work in gold, and in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stone, and in wood, purple and blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson, and to make any engraving and to accomplish any plan that is given to him, with your skilled men and with the skilled men of my master Daviḏ your father.
[15] “And now, the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine which my master has spoken of, let him send to his servants.
[16] “And let us cut wood from Leḇanon, as much as you need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Yapho, and you take it up to Yerushalayim.”

readings.title: The Census of the Strangers
readings.subtitle: Foreign residents within the land are organized to bear the physical burdens of the build.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 2:17] And Shelomoh numbered <dn>את</dn> all the men, the strangers who were in the land of Yisra’ěl, according to the census in which Daviḏ his father had numbered them, and they were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
[18] And he made seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, and eighty thousand hewers of stone in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers to make the people work.

readings.title: Laying the Dimensions
readings.subtitle: Exactly four hundred and eighty years after the Exodus, the architectural framework is erected.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:1] And it came to be, in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yisra’ěl had come out of the land of Mitsrayim, in the fourth year of the reign of Shelomoh over Yisra’ěl, in the new moon of Ziv, which is the second new moon, that he began to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[2] And the house which Sovereign Shelomoh built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was sixty cubits long, and twenty wide, and thirty cubits high.
[3] And the porch at the front of the Hěḵal of the House was twenty cubits long, according to the breadth of the House, and its width ten cubits, from the front of the House.
[4] And he made for the House <dn>את</dn> windows with narrowed frames.

readings.title: The Side Rooms and the Perfect Fit
readings.subtitle: Stones are prepared entirely off-site to ensure absolute silence during the assembly of the House.
readings.text:
[5] And against the wall of the House he built rooms all around, against the walls of the House, all around the Hěḵal and the Speaking Place. Thus he made side rooms all around.
[6] The lowest side room was five cubits wide, and the middle one was six cubits wide, and the third one was seven cubits wide; for he made narrow ledges around the outside of the House, so as not to lay hold on the walls of the House.
[7] And the House, when it was being built, was built with finished stone made ready beforehand, so that no hammer or chisel or any iron tool was heard in the House while it was being built.
[8] The doorway for the middle side room was on the right side of the House. And they went up by stairs to the middle side rooms, and from the middle to the third.
[9] So he built <dn>את</dn> the House and completed it, and he panelled <dn>את</dn> the House with beams and boards of cedar.
[10] And he built <dn>את</dn> the side rooms of the structure against all the House, each five cubits high, and they were fastened to the House with cedar beams.

readings.title: The Divine Condition of Dwelling
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH reminds Shelomoh that the physical structure is meaningless without strict adherence to Torah.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:11] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shelomoh, saying,
[12] <dq>“This House which you are building – if you walk in <dn>My</dn> laws, and do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and shall guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> commands and walk in them, then <dn>I</dn> shall confirm <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> word with <dn>את</dn> you, which <dn>I</dn> spoke to your father Daviḏ,</dq>
[13] <dq>and shall dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl, and not forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl.”</dq>

readings.title: The Anchor of Mount Moriyah
readings.subtitle: Construction is localized precisely where YeHoVaH appeared to Daviḏ at the threshing-floor.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 3:1] And Shelomoh began to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Yerushalayim on Mount Moriyah, where <dn>He</dn> appeared to his father Daviḏ, at the place that Daviḏ had prepared on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
[2] And he began to build on the second day of the second new moon in the fourth year of his reign.
[3] And these are the foundations which Shelomoh laid for building <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>: The length by cubits according to the former measure were sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
[4] And the porch that was in front was twenty cubits long according to the breadth of the house, and the height was one hundred and twenty. And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the inside with clean gold.

readings.title: The Golden Cypress Interior
readings.subtitle: The physical wood is completely shielded by fine gold and precious stones.
readings.text:
[5] And <dn>את</dn> the great house he panelled with cypress which he overlaid with fine gold, and he carved palm trees and chainwork on it.
[6] And he covered <dn>את</dn> the house with precious stones for comeliness, and the gold was gold from Parvayim.
[7] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the house, <dn>את</dn> the beams, <dn>את</dn> the doorposts, and <dn>את</dn> its walls, and <dn>את</dn> its doors with gold, and carved keruḇim on the walls.

readings.title: The Inner Sanctum
readings.subtitle: Six hundred talents of fine gold are committed exclusively to the room of ultimate intersection.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 3:8] And he made <dn>את</dn> the House of the Most Set-apart. Its length was according to the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> it with fine gold, six hundred talents.
[9] And the weight of the nails was fifty sheqels of gold. And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the upper rooms with gold.

readings.title: The Wings of the Keruḇim
readings.subtitle: Massive golden figures are positioned to cover the Speaking Place.
readings.text:
[10] In the Most Set-apart House he made two keruḇim of sculptured work, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> them with gold.
[11] And the wings of the keruḇim: their total length was twenty cubits, one wing was five cubits, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other keruḇ,
[12] and the wing of the other keruḇ was five cubits, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing also was five cubits, touching the wing of the other keruḇ.
[13] The wings of these keruḇim spread out twenty cubits, and they stood on their feet, and they faced inward.
[14] And he made <dn>את</dn> the veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and worked keruḇim on it.

readings.title: Concealing the Stone
readings.subtitle: The stark reality of the stone framework is entirely covered by carved cedar and cypress.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:14] So Shelomoh built <dn>את</dn> the House and completed it.
[15] And he built <dn>את</dn> the walls of the House inside with cedar boards, from the floor of the House to the ceiling he panelled them on the inside with wood, and covered <dn>את</dn> the floor of the House with planks of cypress.
[16] And he built <dn>את</dn> twenty cubits at the rear of the House, from floor to the walls, with cedar boards. And he built it inside as the Speaking Place, as the Most Set-apart Place.
[17] And the House was forty cubits, it is the Hěḵal before it.
[18] And the cedar for the House inside was carved with ornaments and open flowers; all was cedar, not a stone was seen.

readings.title: The Golden Center of Authority
readings.subtitle: The absolute core of the House is sealed with refined gold to receive the Ark of the Covenant.
readings.text:
[19] And he prepared the Speaking Place in the midst of the House, to place the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> there.
[20] And the front of the Speaking Place was twenty cubits long, and twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> it with refined gold, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of cedar.
[21] And Shelomoh overlaid <dn>את</dn> the inside of the House with refined gold, and made gold chains pass over the front of the Speaking Place, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> it with gold.
[22] Thus he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the entire House with gold, until the entire House was completed. And <dn>את</dn> the entire slaughter-place that was by the Speaking Place he overlaid with gold.

readings.title: The Keruḇim of Olive Wood
readings.subtitle: Twin ten-cubit biological representations are stationed with wings spanning the inner walls.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:23] And inside the Speaking Place he made two keruḇim of olive wood, ten cubits high.
[24] And one wing of the keruḇ was five cubits, and the other wing of the keruḇ five cubits – ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
[25] And the other keruḇ was ten cubits. Both keruḇim were of the same size and shape.
[26] The height of one keruḇ was ten cubits, and so was the other keruḇ.
[27] And he placed <dn>את</dn> the keruḇim in the midst of the inner house. And they stretched out the wings of the keruḇim so that the wing of the one touched one wall, and the wing of the other keruḇ touched the other wall. And their wings touched each other in the middle of the room.
[28] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the keruḇim with gold.

readings.title: The Biological and Cosmic Engravings
readings.subtitle: The walls are permanently etched with the living realities of YeHoVaH’s ordered creation.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:29] And he carved <dn>את</dn> all the walls of the House all around, both inside and outside, with carved figures of keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers.
[30] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the floor of the House with gold, inside and outside.

readings.title: The Carved Olive Doors
readings.subtitle: Elaborate folding doors of olive and cypress secure the boundary between the set-apart domains.
readings.text:
[31] And for the entrance of the Speaking Place he made doors of olive wood: the lintel, doorposts, a fifth.
[32] And the two doors were of olive wood. And he carved on them figures of keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> them with gold. And he spread <dn>את</dn> the gold on the keruḇim and on the palm trees.
[33] And so he made doorposts for the door of the Hěḵal of olive wood – a fourth part.
[34] And the two doors were of cypress wood, the two leaves of the one folded, and two leaves of the other door folded.
[35] And he carved keruḇim, and palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold laid smoothly on the carved work.
[36] And he built <dn>את</dn> the inner courtyard with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams.

readings.title: The Seven-Year Completion
readings.subtitle: A perfect cycle of seven years culminates in the exact realization of the divine architectural plans.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 6:37] In the fourth year the foundation of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was laid, in the month Ziv.
[38] And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, the eighth new moon, the house was completed in all its matters and according to all its plans. Thus he built <dn>את</dn> it for seven years.
